1499.subject: Physics
1499.text:
Assertion : The difference in the value of acceleration due to gravity at pole and equator is proportional to square of angular velocity of earth.
Reason : The value of acceleration due to gravity is minimum at the equator and maximum at the pole.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
1499.sol:
Acceleration due to gravity,

g^{\prime}=g-R_e $\omega^$2 \cos ^2 \lambda

At equator, $\lambda=0^{{}^{\circ}}, \quad \therefore \cos 0^{{}^{\circ}}=1$
\therefore $\mathrm{g}_$e=$\mathrm{g}-$R_e $\omega^$2

At poles, $\lambda=90^{{}^{\circ}}, \quad \therefore \cos 90^{{}^{\circ}}=0 \quad \therefore g_p=g$
Thus, $g_p-g_e=g-g+R_e\left(\omega^2=R_e\left(\omega^2\right.\right.$
Also, the value of $g$ is maximum at poles and minimum at equator.

3289.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
3289.text: Identify the element which has highest second ionisation enthalpy.
3289.sol:
As we move across a period, effective nuclear charge $\left(Z_{\text{eff }}\right)$ increases and so do the ionisation energy and moving down a group, effective nuclear charge $\left(Z_{\text{eff }}\right)$ decreases and so do the ionisation energy. So, phosphorus belonging to 3 rd period will have less ionisation energy than 2nd period elements.
Considering the first ionisation energy of 2nd period elements, $\mathrm{N}$ is greater than $\mathrm{O}$ as $\mathrm{N}$ has half-filled stable electronic configuration, but after the removal of 1 electron, oxygen acquires a half-filled stable electronic configuration, the second ionisation potential of oxygen becomes more than of $\mathrm{N} and \mathrm{C}$.

3420.text: Which of the following gives the maximum number of ions in aqueous solution?
3420.sol:
$\mathrm{PtCl}_4 \cdot 6 \mathrm{NH}_3$ [hexammine platinum (IV) chloride]. It gives $4 \mathrm{Cl}^{-}$ ions and $6 \mathrm{NH}_3$, not involved in its ion because $\mathrm{NH}_3$ are present out of the complex of $\mathrm{PtCl}_4$.
$\begin{aligned} & \text{ Hence, } \mathrm{PtCl}_4 \cdot 6 \mathrm{NH}_3 \longrightarrow\left[\mathrm{Pt}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_6\right] \mathrm{Cl}_4 \longrightarrow \\ & \underbrace{\left[\mathrm{Pt}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_6\right]^{4+}+4 \mathrm{Cl}^{-}}_{\text{Total 5 ions }} \\ & \end{aligned}$ In $\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CO})_4, \mathrm{CO}$ is very strong binding ligand, it is difficult to remove all $4 \mathrm{CO}$ from nickel.
On other hand, $\mathrm{CoCl}_3 \cdot 5 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$ dissociates into $\mathrm{Co}^{3+}$, $3 \mathrm{Cl}^{-}$ ions and $5 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$ molecules.
Hence, only $\mathrm{PtCl}_4 \cdot 6 \mathrm{NH}_3$ gives maximum number of ions in aqueous solution.

$\begin{aligned}& f^{\prime}(c)=\frac{f(b)-f(a)}{b-a}=\frac{f\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)-f(0)}{\frac{1}{2}-0}\\
& \Rightarrow \quad 2-3=\frac{\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)\left(-\frac{3}{2}\right)-(-1)(-2)}{-}\\
& \Rightarrow \quad 2 c-3=2\left(\frac{3}{4}-2\right) \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 2 c-3=-\frac{5}{2}\\
& \Rightarrow \quad 4 c-6=-5 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad c=\frac{1}{4} \in\left(0, \frac{1}{2}\right)
\end{aligned}$

& =(4 g-3)^2+(4 f-8)^2 \\

8425.sol:
Given, $\frac{d}{d x}\left[x^{\sin x}+(\sin x)^x\right]$
Let $U=x^{\sin x}, V=(\sin x)^x$
$$
\begin{aligned}
\log U & =\sin x \log x \\
\frac{1}{U} \cdot \frac{d U}{d x} & =\frac{\sin x}{x}+\cos x \log x \\
\frac{d U}{d x} & =x^{\sin x}\left[\frac{\sin x}{x}+\cos x \log x\right]
\end{aligned}
$$
and
$$
V=(\sin x)^x
$$
$$
\begin{aligned}
& \log V=x \log \sin x \\
& \frac{1}{V} \cdot \frac{d V}{d x}=\log \sin x+x \cdot \frac{1}{\sin x} \cos x \\
& \frac{d V}{d x}=(\sin x)^x[\log \sin x+x \cot x] \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \frac{d}{d x}\left[x^{\sin x}+(\sin x)^x\right]=\frac{d U}{d x}+\frac{d V}{d x} \\

(where $C=$ capacitance of capacitor)
When the capacitor is fully discharged, loss of energy is in the form of heat $=\Delta H$ As the system is thermally isolated so,
$\Delta H=\frac{1}{2} C V^2$
Here,
$\Delta H=m s \Delta T\therefore \quad \frac{1}{2} C V^2=m s \Delta T$
or $V=\left(\frac{2 m s \Delta T}{C}\right)^{1 / 2}$

13796.text: Two wooden blocks of mass $M_1$ and $M_2$ rest on a frictionless table. $A$ bullet of mass $m$ is fired at $M_1$ with speed $v$ which embedded in it and the two together finally collide with $M_2$. Find the velocity of $M_2$ after collision. (Ignore any energy loss and treat the problem to be one dimensional)
13796.sol:
( ) For an elastic collision of 2 masses $m_1 and m_2$ with initial velocities $u_1 and u_2$, final velocities of masses after collision are v_1=$\left(\frac{m_1-m_2}{m_1+m_2}\right)u_1+\frac{2 m_2 u_2}{\left(m_1+m_2\right)}$ and v_2=$\left(\frac{m_2-m_1}{m_1+m_2}\right)u_2+\frac{2 m_1 u_2}{m_1+m_2}$ \\ These are obtained as standard results by applying conservation of energy and momentum equations. Now, in given case at first bullet is embedded in mass $M_1$. Let speed of bullet + Block system be $v_1$ after collision.  \\ Then by conservation of momentum we have. $\begin{aligned}& m v=\left(m+M_1\right) v_1 \\
& \text{ or } \quad v_1=\left(\frac{m v}{m+M_1}\right)
\end{aligned}$ Note Here we are not using standard result as first collision is perfectly inelastic.
Now, bullet $+M_1$ strikes $M_2$ and it is given in problem that this collision is elastic.  \\ Now, by formula we have, $\begin{aligned}v_2 & =\left(\frac{  \left(m+M_1\right)-M_2}{m+M_1+M_2}\right)v_1+0 \\
\text{ and, } v_3 \text{ and } =\left(\frac{M_2-  \left(m+M_1\right)}{M_2+m+M_1} \times0\right)+\left(\frac{2\left(m+M_1\right) v_1}{m+M_1+M_2}\right)\\
\Rightarrow \quad v_3 & =\frac{2\left(m+M_1\right)}{m+M_1+M_2} \cdot \frac{m v}{\left(m+M_1\right)}\\
& =\frac{2 m v}{m+M_1+M_2}
\end{aligned}$ Note You can remember these standard and useful results for finding final velocities in case of elastic collisions.

Density of flask's material, ${ρ}_{flask} = \dfrac{m}{V} = \dfrac{390}{140} = 0. 28g{cm}^{- 3}$

Specific gravity of the glass flask is, $= \dfrac{ρflask}{ρwater} = 2. 8$

$⇒ (3,2) \in \mathbb{R}$

So, $R$ is symmetric

Now, $(1,4) \in \mathbb{R}$ and $(4,1) \in \mathbb{R}$

Thus, $R$ is not transitive.

Hence, $R$ is symmetric but neither reflexive nor transitive.

19999.subject: Chemistry
19999.text: The molar conductivity of the complex $\mathrm{CoCl}_3 \cdot 4 \mathrm{NH}_3 \cdot 2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$ is found to be the same as that of a $1: 3$ electrolyte. The structural formula of the compound is :
19999.sol:
The molar conductivity of a $1:3$ electrolyte indicates that the complex dissociates into $4$ ions in total, consisting of one complex cation and three chloride anions. This implies that all three chloride ions are present outside the coordination sphere as counter ions.

The coordination number of Cobalt in such complexes is typically $6$. The formula given is $\mathrm{CoCl}_3 \cdot 4 \mathrm{NH}_3 \cdot 2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$.

If the complex is a $1:3$ electrolyte, the structure must be of the form $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_4(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O})_2]\mathrm{Cl}_3$. In this structure, the coordination sphere contains $4$ ammonia molecules and $2$ water molecules, satisfying the coordination number of $6$. The three chloride ions are outside the coordination sphere, which leads to the dissociation: $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_4(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O})_2]\mathrm{Cl}_3 \rightarrow [\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_4(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O})_2]^{3+} + 3\mathrm{Cl}^{-}$.

This confirms the complex is a $1:3$ electrolyte.

Answer: $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_4\left(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\right)_2\right] \mathrm{Cl}_3$

20487.text: The increasing order of atomic radii of the following group 13 elements is
20487.sol:
The group 13 elements are Boron (B), Aluminium (Al), Gallium (Ga), Indium (In), and Thallium (Tl).

Moving down the group, the atomic radius generally increases due to the addition of new electron shells.

However, there is an anomaly between Aluminium (Al) and Gallium (Ga). Gallium follows the 3d transition series, which contains electrons that provide poor shielding of the nuclear charge. This results in a higher effective nuclear charge for Gallium, causing its atomic radius to be slightly smaller than that of Aluminium.

The atomic radii values are approximately: Al (143 pm), Ga (135 pm), In (167 pm), and Tl (170 pm).

Therefore, the increasing order of atomic radii is $\mathrm{Ga} < \mathrm{Al} < \mathrm{In} < \mathrm{Tl}$.

Answer: $\mathrm{Ga} < \mathrm{Al} < \mathrm{In} < \mathrm{Tl}$

20947.subject: Mathematics
20947.text: $\text{ The rate of change of the volume of a sphere with respect to its surface area } \mathrm{S} \text{$ is }
20947.sol:
Let $r$ be the radius of the sphere. The volume $V$ and surface area $S$ are given by $V = \dfrac{4}{3} \pi r^3$ and $S = 4 \pi r^2$.

From the expression for surface area, $r^2 = \dfrac{S}{4 \pi}$, which implies $r = \sqrt{\dfrac{S}{4 \pi}} = \dfrac{1}{2} \sqrt{\dfrac{S}{\pi}}$.

Differentiating $V$ with respect to $r$, we get $\dfrac{dV}{dr} = 4 \pi r^2$.

Differentiating $S$ with respect to $r$, we get $\dfrac{dS}{dr} = 8 \pi r$.

The rate of change of volume with respect to surface area is $\dfrac{dV}{dS} = \dfrac{dV/dr}{dS/dr} = \dfrac{4 \pi r^2}{8 \pi r} = \dfrac{r}{2}$.

Substituting the value of $r$ in terms of $S$, we get $\dfrac{dV}{dS} = \dfrac{1}{2} \left( \dfrac{1}{2} \sqrt{\dfrac{S}{\pi}} \right) = \dfrac{1}{4} \sqrt{\dfrac{S}{\pi}}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{4} \sqrt{\dfrac{S}{\pi}}$

The function $f(x) = \cos^{-1}(3x - 1)$ is defined when the argument of the inverse cosine function lies in the interval $[-1, 1]$.

Therefore, we set the inequality:

$-1 \le 3x - 1 \le 1$

Adding $1$ to all parts of the inequality:

$-1 + 1 \le 3x - 1 + 1 \le 1 + 1$

$0 \le 3x \le 2$

Dividing by $3$ throughout:

$0 \le x \le \dfrac{2}{3}$

Thus, the domain of $f(x)$ is $[0, \dfrac{2}{3}]$.

Answer: $\left[0, \dfrac{2}{3}\right]$

Subtracting $3(x+y=8)$ from first: $2y = 6 \Rightarrow y = 3,\ x = 5$. Point: $(5,3)$

Other corner points: $(10,0)$ and $(0,8)$.

Evaluating $Z = 150x + 200y$:
At $(10,0)$: $Z = 1500$
At $(5,3)$: $Z = 750 + 600 = 1350$
At $(0,8)$: $Z = 1600$

Since the feasible region is unbounded, verify that no point in the region gives $Z < 1350$. Testing $(6,4)$: $Z = 900 + 800 = 1700 > 1350$. The half-plane $150x + 200y < 1350$ does not intersect the feasible region.

Minimum value of $Z = 1350$ at $(5,3)$.

21746.subject: Mathematics
21746.text:
Matrix $A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & -2 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 & -1 \end{bmatrix}$,
Given $M_{22}$ and $A_{32}$ are the minor and cofactor of the adjoint matrix of A respectively then the value of the expression $M_{22} + A_{32} - |adj\ A|$ is:
21746.sol:
The given matrix is $A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & -2 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 & -1 \end{bmatrix}$.

First, we find the determinant of matrix $A$:
$|A| = 1((-2)(-1) - (2)(0)) - 1((1)(-1) - (2)(1)) + 2((1)(0) - (-2)(1))$
$|A| = 1(2) - 1(-3) + 2(2) = 2 + 3 + 4 = 9$

Using the property of the adjoint of a matrix, $|adj\ A| = |A|^{n-1}$. For a $3 \times 3$ matrix, $n = 3$:
$|adj\ A| = |A|^{3-1} = 9^2 = 81$

Let $B = adj\ A$. We need to find the minor $M_{22}$ and cofactor $A_{32}$ of matrix $B$.
Let $C$ be the cofactor matrix of $B$. By definition, $adj\ B = C^T$, which implies $C = (adj\ B)^T$.

Using the property $adj(adj\ A) = |A|^{n-2}A$, for $n=3$, we have:
$adj\ B = adj(adj\ A) = |A|^{3-2}A = 9A$

Therefore, the cofactor matrix of $B$ is:
$C = (9A)^T = 9A^T$

The cofactor of the $(3,2)$ element of $B$ is $A_{32}$, which is simply $C_{32}$:
$A_{32} = C_{32} = 9(A^T)_{32} = 9A_{23}$
From matrix $A$, the element $A_{23} = 2$.
$A_{32} = 9(2) = 18$

The minor of the $(2,2)$ element of $B$ is $M_{22}$. Since $C_{22} = (-1)^{2+2}M_{22} = M_{22}$, we have:
$M_{22} = C_{22} = 9(A^T)_{22} = 9A_{22}$
From matrix $A$, the element $A_{22} = -2$.
$M_{22} = 9(-2) = -18$

Finally, we evaluate the given expression:
$M_{22} + A_{32} - |adj\ A| = -18 + 18 - 81 = -81$

Answer: $-81$

22528.text: In the diagram shown below, $m_1$ and $m_2$ are the masses of two particles and $x_1$ and $x_2$ are their respective distances from the origin $O$. The centre of mass of the system is
22528.sol:
The position of the centre of mass $X_{cm}$ for a system of particles with masses $m_1, m_2, ..., m_n$ at positions $x_1, x_2, ..., x_n$ along a line is given by the formula:

$X_{cm} = \dfrac{\sum m_i x_i}{\sum m_i}$

For the given system with two particles of masses $m_1$ and $m_2$ at distances $x_1$ and $x_2$ from the origin $O$, the formula becomes:

$X_{cm} = \dfrac{m_1 x_1 + m_2 x_2}{m_1 + m_2}$

Answer: $\dfrac{m_1 x_1+m_2 x_2}{m_1+m_2}$

22717.subject: Physics
22717.text: An AC generator having 400 turns and an area of cross section of $2 \times 10^{-3}\ m^2$ rotates with an angular speed of $200\pi\ rad\ s^{-1}$ in a uniform magnetic field of strength 0.4 T. The generator is connected to the primary of an ideal transformer having 500 turns in the primary and 2000 turns in the secondary. The secondary is connected to a $400\ \Omega$ resistive load. What is the rms current in the secondary of the transformer? Assume, the transformer is ideal and the resistance of the coil is negligible
22717.sol:
The peak emf generated by the AC generator is given by $E_0 = NBA\omega$.

Substituting the given values, $E_0 = 400 \times 0.4 \times (2 \times 10^{-3}) \times 200\pi = 64\pi \text{ V}$.

The rms voltage across the primary coil of the transformer is $V_p = \dfrac{E_0}{\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{64\pi}{\sqrt{2}} \text{ V}$.

For an ideal transformer, the relation between secondary and primary voltages is $\dfrac{V_s}{V_p} = \dfrac{N_s}{N_p}$.

Substituting $N_s = 2000$ and $N_p = 500$, we get $V_s = V_p \times \left( \dfrac{2000}{500} \right) = 4V_p$.

$V_s = 4 \times \dfrac{64\pi}{\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{256\pi}{\sqrt{2}} \text{ V}$.

The rms current in the secondary circuit is $I_s = \dfrac{V_s}{R}$.

$I_s = \dfrac{\dfrac{256\pi}{\sqrt{2}}}{400} = \dfrac{256\pi}{400\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{0.64\pi}{\sqrt{2}} \text{ A}$.

Using the approximation $\pi \approx 3.14$, we get $0.64\pi \approx 2.01 \approx 2$.

$I_s \approx \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{2}} = \sqrt{2} \text{ A}$.

$I_s \approx 1.41 \text{ A}$.

22796.subject: Physics
22796.text: Point charge $\sqrt{2}C, \sqrt{2}C$, and $-2C$ are placed at the three vertices of a right-angled triangle in air. [as shown in the figure below] What is the electric field at a point P on the hypotenuse that is equidistant from all three charges. Given distances $XP = YP = ZP = 0.5\ m$
22796.sol:
Let the charges at vertices $X$, $Y$, and $Z$ be $q_X = \sqrt{2}\ C$, $q_Y = -2\ C$, and $q_Z = \sqrt{2}\ C$ respectively.

Point $P$ is on the hypotenuse $XZ$ and is equidistant from $X$ and $Z$, meaning it is the midpoint of $XZ$.

The electric field at $P$ due to the charge at $X$ is directed away from $X$ (along $PZ$) with magnitude:

$E_X = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0} \dfrac{q_X}{(XP)^2}$

The electric field at $P$ due to the charge at $Z$ is directed away from $Z$ (along $PX$) with magnitude:

$E_Z = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0} \dfrac{q_Z}{(ZP)^2}$

Since $q_X = q_Z = \sqrt{2}\ C$ and $XP = ZP = 0.5\ m$, the magnitudes are equal: $E_X = E_Z$.

As these two fields act in opposite directions along the same line, their vector sum is zero: $\vec{E}_X + \vec{E}_Z = 0$.

The net electric field at $P$ is therefore only due to the charge at $Y$.

Since $q_Y = -2\ C$ is a negative charge, the electric field $\vec{E}_Y$ is directed towards $Y$, which is along the direction $PY$.

The magnitude of the net electric field is:

$E_{net} = E_Y = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0} \dfrac{|q_Y|}{(YP)^2}$

Substituting the given values ($YP = 0.5\ m$ and $\dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0} = 9 \times 10^9\ N m^2 C^{-2}$):

$E_{net} = (9 \times 10^9) \times \dfrac{2}{(0.5)^2}$

$E_{net} = \dfrac{18 \times 10^9}{0.25}$

$E_{net} = 72 \times 10^9\ NC^{-1}$

$E_{net} = 7.2 \times 10^{10}\ NC^{-1}$

Thus, the electric field is $7.2 \times 10^{10}\ NC^{-1}$ along $PY$.

Answer: $7\cdot 2 \times 10^{10}\ NC^{-1}$ along PY

23121.text: The sides of a parallelogram are represented by vectors $\vec{p}=5 \hat{\mathrm{i}}-4 \hat{\mathrm{j}}+3 \hat{\mathrm{k}}$ and $\vec{q}=3 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+2 \hat{\mathrm{j}}-\hat{\mathrm{k}}$. Then, the area of the parallelogram is
23121.sol:
The area of a parallelogram with adjacent sides represented by vectors $\vec{p}$ and $\vec{q}$ is given by the magnitude of their cross product, $|\vec{p} \times \vec{q}|$.

First, calculate the cross product $\vec{p} \times \vec{q}$:
$\vec{p} \times \vec{q} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} \text{ and } \hat{j} \text{ and } \hat{k} \\ 5 \text{ and } -4 \text{ and } 3 \\ 3 \text{ and } 2 \text{ and } -1 \end{vmatrix}$

Expanding the determinant:
$\vec{p} \times \vec{q} = \hat{i}((-4)(-1) - (3)(2)) - \hat{j}((5)(-1) - (3)(3)) + \hat{k}((5)(2) - (-4)(3))$
$\vec{p} \times \vec{q} = \hat{i}(4 - 6) - \hat{j}(-5 - 9) + \hat{k}(10 + 12)$
$\vec{p} \times \vec{q} = -2\hat{i} + 14\hat{j} + 22\hat{k}$

Now, calculate the magnitude of the resulting vector:
$|\vec{p} \times \vec{q}| = \sqrt{(-2)^2 + (14)^2 + (22)^2}$
$|\vec{p} \times \vec{q}| = \sqrt{4 + 196 + 484}$
$|\vec{p} \times \vec{q}| = \sqrt{684}$

The area of the parallelogram is $\sqrt{684} sq units.

Answer: \sqrt{684}$ sq units

23395.text: A beam of parallel rays is brought to a focus by a plano-convex lens. A thin concave lens of the same focal length is joined to the first lens. The effect of this is
options: the focal point shifts away from the lens by a small distance
the focal point shifts towards the lens by a small distance
23395.sol:
The combined focal length of plano-convex lens is $\frac{1}{f}=\frac{1}{f_{1}}+\frac{1}{f_{2}}$ where, $f_{1}=\infty$ for the plane surface and $f_{2}=f \begin{array}{ll}
\therefore \quad$& $\frac{1}{f}=\frac{1}{\infty}+\frac{1}{f}$\\
\Rightarrow \quad f & =f
\end{array} Now, when concave lens of same focal length is joined to first lens, then combined focal length $\begin{array}{ll}
\Rightarrow$& $\frac{1}{F}=\frac{1}{F_{1}}+\frac{1}{F_{2}}$\\
\Rightarrow \quad $\frac{1}{F}$& =$\frac{1}{f}-\frac{1}{f}$\\
\Rightarrow \quad & $\frac{1}{F}=0 \Rightarrow F=$\infty
\end{array}$ Thus, the image can be focused on infinity or focus shifts to infinity.$

23655.subject: Physics
23655.text: Incident light of wavelength $\lambda=800 \mathrm{ nm}$ produces a diffraction pattern on a screen $1.5 \mathrm{ m}$ away when it passes through a single slit of width $0.5 \mathrm{ mm}$. The distance between the first dark fringes on either side of the central bright fringe is
23655.sol:
The condition for the first dark fringe in a single slit diffraction pattern is given by $a \sin \theta = n \lambda$, where $a$ is the slit width, $\lambda$ is the wavelength, and $n = 1$ for the first dark fringe.

Since $\theta$ is very small, $\sin \theta \approx \tan \theta = \dfrac{y}{D}$, where $y$ is the distance of the fringe from the central maximum and $D$ is the distance to the screen.

Substituting the values: $a \left( \dfrac{y}{D} \right) = \lambda \Rightarrow y = \dfrac{\lambda D}{a}$.

Given $\lambda = 800 \text{ nm} = 800 \times 10^{-9} \text{ m}$, $D = 1.5 \text{ m}$, and $a = 0.5 \text{ mm} = 0.5 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}$.

$y = \dfrac{800 \times 10^{-9} \times 1.5}{0.5 \times 10^{-3}} = \dfrac{1200 \times 10^{-9}}{0.5 \times 10^{-3}} = 2400 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m} = 2.4 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m} = 2.4 \text{ mm}$.

The distance between the first dark fringes on either side of the central bright fringe is $2y = 2 \times 2.4 \text{ mm} = 4.8 \text{ mm}$.

Answer: 4.8 mm

23977.subject: Chemistry
23977.text: Which one of the following molecules shows an increase in bond order after loss of an electron from the highest occupied molecular orbital?
23977.sol: Bond order is given by $\dfrac{1}{2}(N_b - N_a)$. If an electron is removed from an antibonding molecular orbital, $N_a$ decreases, resulting in an increase in bond order. If it is removed from a bonding molecular orbital, $N_b$ decreases, resulting in a decrease in bond order. The molecular orbital electronic configurations are: $\text{F}_2$ (18 electrons): $\sigma_{1s}^{2} \sigma_{1s}^{*2} \sigma_{2s}^{2} \sigma_{2s}^{*2} \sigma_{2p_z}^{2} \pi_{2p_x}^{2} \pi_{2p_y}^{2} \pi_{2p_x}^{*2} \pi_{2p_y}^{*2}$ The highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) is $\pi_{2p}^{*}$, which is antibonding. Loss of an electron decreases $N_a$, increasing the bond order from $1$ to $1.5$. $\text{N}_2$ (14 electrons): $\sigma_{1s}^{2} \sigma_{1s}^{*2} \sigma_{2s}^{2} \sigma_{2s}^{*2} \pi_{2p_x}^{2} \pi_{2p_y}^{2} \sigma_{2p_z}^{2}$ The HOMO is $\sigma_{2p_z}$, which is bonding. Loss of an electron decreases $N_b$, decreasing the bond order from $3$ to $2.5$. $\text{C}_2$ (12 electrons): $\sigma_{1s}^{2} \sigma_{1s}^{*2} \sigma_{2s}^{2} \sigma_{2s}^{*2} \pi_{2p_x}^{2} \pi_{2p_y}^{2}$ The HOMO is $\pi_{2p}$, which is bonding. Loss of an electron decreases $N_b$, decreasing the bond order from $2$ to $1.5$. $\text{B}_2$ (10 electrons): $\sigma_{1s}^{2} \sigma_{1s}^{*2} \sigma_{2s}^{2} \sigma_{2s}^{*2} \pi_{2p_x}^{1} \pi_{2p_y}^{1}$ The HOMO is $\pi_{2p}$, which is bonding. Loss of an electron decreases $N_b$, decreasing the bond order from $1$ to $0.5$. Thus, only $\text{F}_2$ shows an increase in bond order. Answer: $\text{F}_2$

27696.subject: Chemistry
27696.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : The number of compounds among SO$_2$, SO$_3$, SF$_4$, SF$_6$ and H$_2$S in which sulphur does not obey the Octet rule is $3$.
Statement II : Among [H$_2$O, ClF$_3$, SF$_4$], [NH$_3$, BrF$_5$, SF$_4$], [BrF$_5$, ClF$_3$, XeF$_4$] and [XeF$_4$, ClF$_3$, H$_2$O], the number of sets in which all the molecules have one lone pair of electrons on the central atom is $1$.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
27696.sol:
Statement I: Number of compounds in which sulphur does not follow the octet rule (from $SO_2$, $SO_3$, $SF_4$, $SF_6$ and $H_2S$).

$SO_2$: The formal-charge-minimised structure $O=S=O$ places $10$ electrons around sulphur (expanded octet).
$SO_3$: With three $S=O$ double bonds, sulphur has $12$ electrons around it (expanded octet).
$SF_4$: $4$ bond pairs $+ 1$ lone pair $= 10$ electrons around $S$ (expanded octet).
$SF_6$: $6$ bond pairs $= 12$ electrons around $S$ (expanded octet).
$H_2S$: $2$ bond pairs $+ 2$ lone pairs $= 8$ electrons around $S$ (obeys the octet rule).

Depending on whether formal-charge-minimised structures are used for $SO_2$ and $SO_3$, either $2$ ($SF_4, SF_6$) or $4$ ($SO_2, SO_3, SF_4, SF_6$) species violate the octet rule, but the number is never $3$.
Hence, Statement I is false.

Statement II: Among the given sets, exactly one contains only molecules having one lone pair on the central atom.

Number of lone pairs on the central atom, $\text{LP} = \dfrac{\text{valence electrons of central atom} - \text{number of bonded monovalent atoms}}{2}$:

$H_2O$: $\dfrac{6 - 2}{2} = 2$ lone pairs
$ClF_3$: $\dfrac{7 - 3}{2} = 2$ lone pairs
$SF_4$: $\dfrac{6 - 4}{2} = 1$ lone pair
$NH_3$: $\dfrac{5 - 3}{2} = 1$ lone pair
$BrF_5$: $\dfrac{7 - 5}{2} = 1$ lone pair
$XeF_4$: $\dfrac{8 - 4}{2} = 2$ lone pairs

Checking the sets:
$\{H_2O\ (2),\ ClF_3\ (2),\ SF_4\ (1)\}$: not all have $1$ lone pair.
$\{NH_3\ (1),\ BrF_5\ (1),\ SF_4\ (1)\}$: all have exactly $1$ lone pair.
$\{BrF_5\ (1),\ ClF_3\ (2),\ XeF_4\ (2)\}$: not all have $1$ lone pair.
$\{XeF_4\ (2),\ ClF_3\ (2),\ H_2O\ (2)\}$: not all have $1$ lone pair.

Exactly one set satisfies the condition, so Statement II is true.

Hence, Statement I is false but Statement II is true, which corresponds to option $(4)$.

28020.subject: Chemistry
28020.text:
Dissociation of a gas $\mathrm{A}_{2}$ takes place according to the following chemical reaction. At equilibrium, the total pressure is 1 bar at 300 K.
$\mathrm{A}_{2}(\mathrm{~g}) \rightleftharpoons 2 \mathrm{~A}(\mathrm{~g})
The standard Gibbs energy of formation of $the involved substances has been provided below:
\(
Substance\Delta G_{f}^{\circ} / kJ mol^{-1}
A_2-100.00
A-50.832
\)
The degree of dissociation of$\mathrm{A}_{2}(\mathrm{~g})$ is given by $\left(x \times 10^{-2}\right)^{1 / 2}$ where $x= \_\_\_\_$. (Nearest integer).
[Given: $\mathrm{R}=8 \mathrm{~J} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1} \mathrm{~K}^{-1}, \log 2=0.3010, \log 3=0.48$ ]
Assume degree of dissociation is not negligible.
28020.sol:
For the dissociation reaction $A_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2A(g)$, first calculate the standard Gibbs free energy:
$\Delta G°_{rxn} = 2(-50.832) - (-100.00) = -1.664$ kJ/mol.
Using $\Delta G° = -RT \ln K_p$:
$-1664 = -8 \times 300 \times \ln K_p$, giving $K_p = e^{0.6933} = 2$.
For dissociation with degree of dissociation $\alpha$, starting with 1 mole of $A_2$ at 1 bar total pressure:
At equilibrium, moles are $(1-\alpha)$ for $A_2$ and $2\alpha$ for $A$, with total $(1+\alpha)$ moles.
$K_p = \frac{4\alpha^2}{1-\alpha^2} = 2$.
Solving: $2(1-\alpha^2) = 4\alpha^2$ gives $\alpha^2 = 1/3$ or $\alpha = 0.577$.
Since degree of dissociation is $(x \times 10^{-2})^{1/2}$:
$(x \times 10^{-2})^{1/2} = 0.577$ gives $x \times 10^{-2} = 0.333$, so $x = 33.3 \approx 33$.

Another ${Co}^{3 +}$ complex, $[ Co{( CN )}_{6}{]}^{3 -}$, is diamagnetic and has no unpaired electrons. The hybrid orbitals used to form this complex are ${d}^{2}{sp}^{3}$.

32420.subject: Chemistry
32420.text:
Match List-I and List-II

List-I List-II
A. Osmosis I. Solvent molecules pass through semi permeable membrane towards solvent side.
B. Reverse osmosis II. Movement of charged colloidal particles under the influence of applied electric potential towards oppositely charged electrodes
C. Electro osmosis III. Solvent molecules pass through semi permeable membrane towards solution side
D. Electrophoresis IV. Dispersion medium moves in an electric field.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
32420.sol:
(A) Osmosis: It is a process by which the molecules of a solvent pass from a solution of low concentration to a solution of high concentration through a semi-permeable membrane.

(B) Reverse osmosis: The direction of osmosis can be reversed if a pressure larger than the osmotic pressure is applied to the solution side. Now the pure solvent flows out of the solution through the semi-permeable membrane. This phenomenon is called reverse osmosis.

(C) Electroosmosis: When electrophoresis, i.e., movement of particles is prevented by some suitable means, it is observed that the dispersion medium begins to move in an electric field. This phenomenon is termed electroosmosis.

(D) Electrophoresis: When an electric potential is applied across two platinum electrodes dipping in a colloidal solution, the colloidal particles move towards one or the other electrode. The movement of colloidal particles under an applied electric potential is called electrophoresis.

So the correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

$I = - \dfrac{24}{\pi}{∫}_{\infty}^{2\sqrt{2}}\dfrac{dt}{t\sqrt{{t}^{2} - 4}} = - \dfrac{12}{\pi}{∫}_{\infty}^{2\sqrt{2}}\dfrac{2tdt}{{t}^{2}\sqrt{{t}^{2} - 4}}$

Let ${t}^{2} - 4 = {z}^{2}, 2tdt = 2zdz$

35431.text: The locus of the centroid of the triangle formed by any point $P$ on the hyperbola $16{x}^{2} - 9{y}^{2} + 32x + 36y - 164 = 0$ and its foci is
35431.sol:
Given hyperbola is

$16{x}^{2} - 9{y}^{2} + 32x + 36y - 164 = 0$

$⇒ 16{\left(x + 1\right)}^{2} - 9{\left(y - 2\right)}^{2} = 164 + 16 - 36$

$⇒ 16{\left(x + 1\right)}^{2} - 9{\left(y - 2\right)}^{2} = 144 . . . . \left(1\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{( x + 1{)}^{2}}{9} - \dfrac{( y - 2{)}^{2}}{16} = 1$

Compare the above equation with $⇒ \dfrac{( x - h{)}^{2}}{{a}^{2}} - \dfrac{( y - k{)}^{2}}{{b}^{2}} = 1$

We get, $h = - 1, k = 2, {a}^{2} = 9 and {b}^{2} = 16$

$∴$ Eccentricity, $e = \sqrt{1 + \dfrac{16}{9}} = \dfrac{5}{3}$

We know that, focii are $\left(h + ae, k\right)$ and $\left(h - ae, k\right)$

Hence, focii are $( 4, 2 ) and ( - 6, 2 )$

Let the centroid be $( h, k )$ & $A ( \alpha, \beta )$ be point on hyperbola

So $h = \dfrac{\alpha - 6 + 4}{3}, k = \dfrac{\beta + 2 + 2}{3}$

$⇒ \alpha = 3h + 2, \beta = 3k - 4$

Put the values of $\alpha, \beta$ in the equation$\left(1\right)$,

$16{\left(\left(3h + 2\right) + 1\right)}^{2} - 9{\left(\left(3k - 4\right) - 2\right)}^{2} = 144$

$⇒ 144 ( h + 1{)}^{2} - 81 ( k - 2{)}^{2} = 144$

$⇒ 16\left({h}^{2} + 2h + 1\right) - 9\left({k}^{2} - 4k + 4\right) = 16$

$⇒ 16{h}^{2} - 9{k}^{2} + 32h + 36k - 36 = 0$

So, the locus of the centroid is

$16{x}^{2} - 9{y}^{2} + 32x + 36y - 36 = 0$

37415.text: Let $A = \left\{1, 2, 3, 4\right\}$ and $R = \left\{( 1, 2 ) , ( 2, 3 ) , ( 1, 4 )\right\}$ be a relation on $A$. Let $S$ be the equivalence relation on $A$ such that $R ⊂ S$ and the number of elements in $S$ is $n$. Then, the minimum value of $n$ is _______
37415.sol:
Given,

$A = \left\{1, 2, 3, 4\right\}$ and $R =\left\{( 1, 2 ) , ( 2, 3 ) , ( 1, 4 )\right\}$ be a relation on $A$.

Now, given $S$ be the equivalence relation on $A and R ⊂ S$

So, for $S$ to be equivalence it should be Reflexive, Symmetric and Transitive on given relation,

Now, for reflexive Relation we need, $\left\{\left(1, 1\right), \left(2, 2\right), \left(3, 3\right), \left(4, 4\right)\right\} \to 4$ elements,

For Symmetric relation we need, $\left\{\left(2, 1\right), \left(3, 2\right), \left(4, 1\right)\right\} \to 3$ elements,

And for Transitive relation we need, $\left\{\left(1, 3\right), \left(3, 1\right), \left(3, 4\right), \left(4, 2\right), \left(2, 4\right), \left(4, 3\right)\right\} \to 6$ elements

So, minimum $13$ elements should be added in $R$

Hence , $n\left(S\right) = 16$ elements.

37883.text: The square of the distance of the point $P(5, 6, 7)$ from the line $\dfrac{x-2}{2} = \dfrac{y-5}{3} = \dfrac{z-2}{4}$ is equal to:
37883.sol:
Let the foot of the perpendicular from $P(5, 6, 7)$ to the given line be $Q$.

Any point on the line $\dfrac{x-2}{2} = \dfrac{y-5}{3} = \dfrac{z-2}{4} = \lambda$ is $Q(2\lambda + 2, 3\lambda + 5, 4\lambda + 2)$.

The direction ratios of $PQ$ are $(2\lambda - 3, 3\lambda - 1, 4\lambda - 5)$.

Since $PQ$ is perpendicular to the line, the dot product of their direction ratios is zero:

$2(2\lambda - 3) + 3(3\lambda - 1) + 4(4\lambda - 5) = 0$

$4\lambda - 6 + 9\lambda - 3 + 16\lambda - 20 = 0$

$29\lambda - 29 = 0 \Rightarrow \lambda = 1$

Substituting $\lambda = 1$, the coordinates of $Q$ are $(4, 8, 6)$.

The square of the distance $PQ^2$ is $(5 - 4)^2 + (6 - 8)^2 + (7 - 6)^2 = 1 + 4 + 1 = 6$.

Answer: $6$

Match the List-I with List-II:

List I List II
A Microwaves I Radioactive decay of the nucleus
B Gamma rays II Rapid acceleration and deceleration of electron in aerials
C Radio waves III Inner shell electrons
D X-rays IV Klystron valve

40322.sol:
(A) A Klystron valve or the magnetron valve are generally used for the production of electromagnetic waves and that electromagnetic wave is Microwave. So, $\left(A\right) \to IV$.

(B) Gamma rays are produced during the disintegration of radioactive atomic nuclei and the decay of certain subatomic particles.So, $\left(B\right) \to I$

(C) Radio waves can be produced by rapid acceleration and deceleration of electrons in aerials (conductors). These can be detected by receivers of aerials. So, $\left(C\right) \to II$

(D) X-rays are produced when a metal target or any other element is bombarded with high energy particles such as electrons, photons or ions. When high energy electrons is incident on a bound electron in an atom, then bound electron emits from the inner shell of that atom. So, $\left(D\right) \to III$

46480.text: Two radioactive substances $A and B$ have decay constants $5 \lambda$ and $\lambda$ respectively. At $t=0$ they have the same number of nuclei. The ratio of number of nuclei of $A$ to those of $B$ will be $\left(\frac{1}{e}\right)^2$ after a time interval
46480.sol:
Number of nuclei remained after time $t$ can be written as
$N=N_0 e^{-\lambda t}$
where $N_0$ is initial number of nuclei of both the substances.
and
$\begin{aligned}
& N_1=N_0 e^{-5 \lambda t} \ldots(i)\\
& N_2=N_0 e^{-\lambda t} \ldots(ii)
\end{aligned}$
Dividing Eq. (i) by Eq. (ii), we obtain
$\frac{N_1}{N_2}=e^{(-5 \lambda+\lambda) t}=e^{-4 \lambda t}=\frac{1}{e^{4 \lambda t}}$
But, we have given
$\frac{N_1}{N_2}=\left(\frac{1}{e}\right)^2=\frac{1}{e^2}$
Hence, $\quad \frac{1}{e^2}=\frac{1}{e^{4 \lambda t}}$
Comparing the powers, we get
or
$\begin{aligned}
& 2=4 \lambda t \\
& t=\frac{2}{4 \lambda}=\frac{1}{2 \lambda}
\end{aligned}$

47336.text:
Arrange the following compounds in the increasing order of their acidic strength :
i. m-nitrophenol
ii. m-cresol
iii. phenol
iv. m-chlorophenol
47336.sol:
Nitro group has both \( -R \) effect and \( -1 \) effect; but \( -R \) effect predominates. Due to stronger electron withdrawing nature of
\( \mathrm{NO}_{2} \) group, phenoxide ion is stabilized. Hence, m-nitrophenol is more acidic than phenol. Methyl group destabilizes the
phenoxide ion by \( +I \) effect and hyperconjugation. Hence m-cresol is weaker acid than phenol. Chlorine have both +R
and \( -1 \) effect but \( -1 \) effect predominates
Hence m-chlorophenol is more acidic than phenol. \( -R \) effect of nitro group is stronger than \( -1 \) effect of chlorine hence, m-
nitrophenol is more acidic than m-chlorophenol.
Therefore, the correct order of acidic strength is \( m \)-nitrophenol \( >m \)-chlorophenol \( >p h e n o l>m \)-cresol.



(II)
(III)
(IV)
(I)

47853.text: The number of chain isomers possible for the hydrocarbon with molecular formula $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{12}$ is
47853.sol:
The given molecular formula is $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{12}$, which corresponds to an alkane (pentane).

The possible chain isomers are:

1. n-pentane: $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3$

2. isopentane (2-methylbutane): $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3$

3. neopentane (2,2-dimethylpropane): $\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)_4$

Thus, there are $3$ chain isomers possible for $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{12}$.

Answer: $3$

50152.text:
For which combination of working temperatures, the efficiency of 'Carnot's engine' is the least
\( ? \)
50152.sol:
Efficiency of Carnot's engine is given as
\( \eta=1-$\frac{T_{2}}{T_{1}}$\)
For \( T_{1}=60 $\mathrm{~K}$\) and \( T_{2}=40 $\mathrm{~K}, \eta=$1-$\frac{40}{60}=$0.333 \)
For \( T_{1}=40 $\mathrm{~K}$\) and \( T_{2}=20 $\mathrm{~K}, \eta=$1-$\frac{20}{40}=$0.5 \)
For \( T_{1}=80 K \) and \( T_{2}=60 K, \eta=1-$\frac{60}{80}=$0.25 \)
For \( T_{1}=100 $\mathrm{~K}$\) and \( T_{2}=80 $\mathrm{~K}, \eta=$1-$\frac{80}{100}=$0.2 \)
Therefore, the efficiency of Carnot's engine is the least for \( T_{1}=100 $\mathrm{~K}$\) and \( T_{2}=80 $\mathrm{~K}$\)

50282.text: A cyclotron is used to accelerate protons $\left({ }_{1}^{1} \mathrm{H}\right)$ deuterons $\left({ }_{1}^{2} \mathrm{H}\right)$ and $\alpha$-particles $\left({ }_{2}^{4} \mathrm{He}\right)$. While exiting under similar conditions, the minimum KE is gained by
50282.sol:
When a charged particle is accelerated by a potential difference $V$ volts, then the radius of the trajectory of the path of the particle is given as,
$\begin{aligned}
r &=\frac{\sqrt{2 K m}}{B q}=\frac{\sqrt{2 q V m}}{B q} \\
\Rightarrow \quad K &=\frac{1}{2} \frac{B^{2} q^{2} r^{2}}{m} \text{ or } K \propto \frac{q^{2}}{m} ...(i)
\end{aligned}$
For protons $\left({ }_{1}^{1} \mathrm{H}\right)$, deuterons $\left({ }_{1}^{2} \mathrm{H}\right)$ and $\alpha$-particles $\left({ }_{2}^{4} \mathrm{He}\right)$,
$\begin{aligned} q_{p}: q_{d}: q_{\alpha} &=1: 1: 2 ...(ii)\\ m_{p}: m_{d}: m_{\alpha} &=1: 2: 4 ...(iii)\end{aligned}$
From Eqs. (i), (ii) and (iii), we can write
$\Rightarrow \quad K_{p}: K_{d}: K_{\alpha}=1: \frac{1}{4}: 1$
Thus, minimum kinetic energy is gained by deuterons.

50546.subject: Physics
50546.text: The incorrect statement about refractive index for a pair of media is
options: It depends upon nature of the first medium.
It depends upon nature of the second medium.
It depends upon wavelength of light
It depends upon angle of incidence
50546.sol:
The refractive index of a second medium with respect to a first medium is defined as the ratio of the speed of light in the first medium to the speed of light in the second medium, given by $n_{21} = \dfrac{v_1}{v_2}$.

The speed of light in a medium depends on the optical properties (nature) of that medium and the wavelength of the light used (due to dispersion). Therefore, the refractive index for a pair of media depends on the nature of both the first and second media, as well as the wavelength of the light.

According to Snell's law, the ratio $\dfrac{\sin i}{\sin r}$ is a constant for a given pair of media and a given wavelength of light. This constant is the refractive index, which remains independent of the angle of incidence.

Thus, the statement that refractive index depends upon the angle of incidence is incorrect.

Answer: It depends upon angle of incidence

52149.text: The potential due to an electrostatic charge distribution is $V\left(r\right) = \dfrac{qe^{- \alphar}}{4\pi{ε}_{0}r},$ where $\alpha$ is positive. The net charge within a sphere centred at the origin and of radius $1 / \alpha$ is
52149.sol:
Electric field due to given charge distribution is

$E = - \dfrac{dV}{dr} = - \dfrac{d}{dr}\dfrac{q{e}^{- \alphar}}{4\pi{ε}_{0}r}$

$= \dfrac{- q}{4\pi{ε}_{0}}\dfrac{d}{dr}\left(\dfrac{{e}^{- \alphar}}{r}\right)$

$= \dfrac{- q}{4\pi{ε}_{0}}\left(\dfrac{- \alphar{e}^{- \alphar} - {e}^{- \alphar}}{{r}^{2}}\right)$

$= \dfrac{q}{4\pi{ε}_{0}} \cdot {e}^{- \alphar} \cdot \left(\dfrac{\alphar + 1}{{r}^{2}}\right)$

Electric field at $r = \dfrac{1}{\alpha}$ is

$E\left(r = \dfrac{1}{\alpha}\right) = \dfrac{q}{4\pi{ε}_{0}} \cdot {e}^{- \alpha \times \dfrac{1}{\alpha}}\left(\dfrac{\alpha \times \dfrac{1}{\alpha} + 1}{1 / {\alpha}^{2}}\right)$

$= \dfrac{\left(q / e\right)}{4\pi{ε}_{0}} \cdot 2{\alpha}^{2}$

Flux through a sphere of radius $\dfrac{1}{\alpha}$ is

$ϕ = ∫ E \cdot dA$

For spherical distribution,
$E \cdot dA = EdAcos0 ° = EdA$
and $E =$ uniform.
So, we have

$∴ ϕ = E ∫ dA$

$= \dfrac{q / e}{4\pi{ε}_{0}} \cdot 2{\alpha}^{2} \cdot 4\pi{\left(\dfrac{1}{\alpha}\right)}^{2}$

or $ϕ = \dfrac{2q}{{ε}_{0}e}$

From Gauss' law, we have $ϕ = \dfrac{{q}_{enclosed}}{{ε}_{0}}$

So, charge enclosed in given sphere is $\dfrac{2q}{e}$

54840.subject: Chemistry
54840.text: Which of the following isomers of $\text{C}_4\text{H}_9\text{OH}$ has lowest boiling point ?
54840.sol:
The boiling point of isomeric alcohols decreases with an increase in branching.

As branching increases, the molecule becomes more spherical in shape, which decreases the effective surface area.

A smaller surface area results in weaker van der Waals forces of attraction between the molecules, thereby lowering the boiling point.

Among the given isomers of $\text{C}_4\text{H}_9\text{OH}$, tert-butyl alcohol is the most branched.

Therefore, tert-butyl alcohol has the lowest boiling point.

Answer: tert Butyl alcohol

Using the rate law $r = k[A]^2[B]$ with $k = 6.25 \mathrm{M}^{-2} \mathrms^{-1}$, $[A] = 1 \mathrm{M}$, and $[B] = 0.2 \mathrm{M}$:

$r = (6.25) \times (1)^2 \times (0.2)$

The numerical calculation yields $6.25 \times 0.2 = 1.25$, while dimensional analysis gives $\mathrm{M}^{-2} \cdot \mathrm{M}^2 \cdot \mathrm{M} = \mathrm{M}$.

Thus $r = 1.25 \mathrm{M} \mathrms^{-1}$ or equivalently $1.25 \mathrm{mol} \mathrm{dm}^{-3} \mathrms^{-1}$, matching option A.

57132.subject: Chemistry
57132.text: Which of the following is NOT a phenol ?
57132.sol:
A phenol is a compound in which a hydroxyl group ($-OH$) is directly attached to an $sp^2$ hybridized carbon atom of an aromatic ring.

In the first option, the $-OH$ group is directly attached to the benzene ring (o-nitrophenol), so it is a phenol.

In the second option, the $-OH$ group is directly attached to the naphthalene ring (2-naphthol), so it is considered a phenolic compound.

In the third option, the $-OH$ group is directly attached to the benzene ring (o-bromophenol), so it is a phenol.

In the fourth option, the $-OH$ group is attached to an $sp^3$ hybridized carbon atom of a side chain ($-CH_2OH$), not directly to the aromatic ring. This compound is benzyl alcohol, which is an aromatic alcohol but not a phenol.

Answer:

57157.subject: Chemistry
57157.text: What is IUPAC name of the compound $\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CHCH=CHCOOH}$ ?
57157.sol:
The principal functional group is the carboxylic acid ($-\text{COOH}$), so numbering starts from the carbon atom of the $-\text{COOH}$ group.

The longest carbon chain containing the principal functional group has $6$ carbon atoms, so the root word is 'hex'.

There are two double bonds located at C2 and C4, so the primary suffix is '2,4-diene'.

The secondary suffix for the carboxylic acid is 'oic acid'.

Combining these parts, the IUPAC name of the compound is Hexa-2,4-dienoic acid.

Answer: Hexa-2,4-dienoic acid

58009.subject: Chemistry
58009.text: Which among the following salt turns blue litmus red in its aqueous solution?
58009.sol:
Identification of acidic salt

The salt that turns blue litmus red must yield an acidic aqueous solution through hydrolysis of its constituent ions.

Copper(II) sulfate ($\mathrm{CuSO4}$) dissociates into $\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}$ and $\mathrm{SO_4^{2-}}$ ions. The $\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}$ cation, being the conjugate acid of weak base $\mathrm{Cu(OH)_2}$, hydrolyzes:
$\mathrm{Cu^{2+} + 2H_2 O < = > Cu(OH)_2 + 2H+}$
This reaction produces hydrogen ions, acidifying the solution.

Sodium carbonate ($\mathrm{Na_2CO_3}$) yields basic solution due to $\mathrm{CO_3^{2-}}$ hydrolysis: $\mathrm{CO_3^{2-} + H_2 O < = > HCO_3- + OH-}$.

Sodium sulfate ($\mathrm{Na_2SO_4}$) and sodium nitrate ($\mathrm{NaNO_3}$) form neutral solutions as both ions derive from strong acid-base pairs and undergo negligible hydrolysis.

$\mathrm{CuSO_4}$ is the only salt producing acidic solution that turns blue litmus red.

59649.subject: Chemistry
59649.text: $Calculate the energy per mole of photon of electromagnetic radiation having wave length 700 nm  \left[\mathrm{h}=6.626 \times 10^{-34} \mathrm{Js}, \mathrm{C}=3 \times 10^8 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm{s}\right]$
59649.sol:
Energy per mole of photons is calculated from the energy of a single photon multiplied by Avogadro's number.

The energy of a photon is given by $E = \frac{hc}{\lambda}$, where Planck's constant $h = 6.626 \times 10^{-34} \mathrm{Js}$, the speed of light $c = 3 \times 10^8 \mathrm{m/s}$, and wavelength $\lambda = 700 \,\mathrm{nm} = 7 \times 10^{-7} \,\mathrm{m}$.

Substituting these values:
$E = \frac{(6.626 \times 10^{-34}) \cdot (3 \times 10^8)}{7 \times 10^{-7}} = 2.8397 \times 10^{-19} \,\mathrm{J}$.

Multiplying by Avogadro's number $N_{\mathrm{A}} = 6.022 \times 10^{23} \,\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ gives the energy per mole:
$E_{\mathrm{mole}} = (2.8397 \times 10^{-19}) \cdot (6.022 \times 10^{23}) = 1.7109 \times 10^5 \,\mathrm{J/mol}$.

Rounded to three significant figures, the value is $1.71 \times 10^5 \,\mathrm{J/mol}$.

Among the options, A) $1.71 \times 10^5 \,\mathrm{J}$ matches this result.

$\boxed{\mathrm{A}}$

59676.sol:
The lowest transition in Balmer series is from $\mathrm{n}_1=2$ and $\mathrm{n}_2=3$
$\therefore \quad \overline{\mathrm{v}}=\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{H}}\left[\frac{1}{\mathrm{n}_1{ }^2}-\frac{1}{\mathrm{n}_2^2}\right]=\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{H}}\left[\frac{1}{2^2}-\frac{1}{3^2}\right]=\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{H}}\left[\frac{5}{36}\right]$

60723.subject: Mathematics
60723.text: If one of the diameters of the circle, given by the equation $x^2+y^2-4 x+6 y-12=0$, is a chord of a circle, 'S', whose centre is at $(-3,2)$, then the length of radius of ' $S$ ' is ______ units.
60723.sol:
Find the radius of circle $S$ given its center at $(-3,2)$ and that a diameter of $C_1$ is a chord of $S$.

For circle $C_1$ defined by $x^2+y^2-4x+6y-12=0$, comparing with the general form $x^2+y^2+2gx+2fy+c=0$ gives $g = -2$, $f = 3$, and $c = -12$.

The center of $C_1$ is $(2,-3)$ and its radius is $r_1 = \sqrt{g^2+f^2-c} = \sqrt{4+9+12} = 5$.

The diameter of $C_1$ has length $10$ and serves as a chord of $S$. The perpendicular distance from the center of $S$ at $(-3,2)$ to this chord is the distance to the midpoint $(2,-3)$: $d = \sqrt{(2+3)^2+(-3-2)^2} = \sqrt{25+25} = 5\sqrt{2}$.

Using the right triangle formed by the center of $S$, the chord midpoint, and an endpoint, apply the Pythagorean theorem: $R^2 = d^2 + \left(\frac{10}{2}\right)^2 = (5\sqrt{2})^2 + 5^2 = 50 + 25 = 75$.

$R = \sqrt{75} = 5\sqrt{3}$

Final answer: $\boxed{C}$

60787.subject: Mathematics
60787.text: The equation of tangent to the circle $x^2+y^2=64$ at the point $\mathrm{P}\left(\frac{2 \pi}{3}\right)$ is
60787.sol:
Circle $x^2+y^2=(8)^2$, has radius 8 and centre $(0,0)$. Point $\mathrm{P}\left(\frac{2 \pi}{3}\right)$ on the circle has coordinates
$$
\mathrm{P} \equiv\left(8 \cos \frac{2 \pi}{3}, 8 \sin \frac{2 \pi}{3}\right) \text { i.e. } \mathrm{P} \equiv(-4,4 \sqrt{3})
$$
Differentiating equation of circle w.r.t. $\mathrm{x}$, we get
$$
2 x+2 y \frac{d y}{d x}=0 \Rightarrow \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{-x}{y} \Rightarrow\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)_P=\frac{4}{4 \sqrt{3}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}
$$
Hence required equation of tangent is
$$
(\mathrm{y}-4 \sqrt{3})=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}(\mathrm{x}+4) \Rightarrow \mathrm{x}-\sqrt{3} \mathrm{y}+16=0
$$

61304.text: The particular solution of the differential equation $xdy + 2ydx = 0$, when $x = 2$ and $y = 1$ is
61304.sol:
The given differential equation is $xdy + 2ydx = 0$

Separating the variables, we get:

$\dfrac{dy}{y} + \dfrac{2dx}{x} = 0$

Integrating both sides:

$\int \dfrac{dy}{y} + 2 \int \dfrac{dx}{x} = 0$

$\ln y + 2 \ln x = \ln C$

$\ln(y x^2) = \ln C$

$x^2 y = C$

Substituting $x = 2$ and $y = 1$:

$(2)^2(1) = C \Rightarrow C = 4$

The particular solution is $x^2 y = 4$

Taking the square root on both sides:

$x\sqrt{y} = \pm 2$

Since $x = 2$ and $y = 1$ satisfies the positive root, we get:

$x\sqrt{y} = 2$

Answer: $x\sqrt{y} = 2$

61305.subject: Mathematics
61305.text:
The population $p$ of the city at time $t$ is given by $\frac{d p}{d t}=\frac{p}{2}-100$.
If initial population is 100 then $\mathrm{p}=$
61305.sol:
The differential equation $\frac{dp}{dt} = \frac{p}{2} - 100$ with initial condition $p(0) = 100$ is separable.
Rewriting gives $\frac{dp}{dt} = \frac{p - 200}{2}$, leading to $\frac{dp}{p - 200} = \frac{1}{2} dt$.
Integrating both sides yields $\ln|p - 200| = \frac{1}{2}t + C$.

Exponentiating produces $|p - 200| = e^{C}e^{t/2}$.
The general solution is $p(t) = 200 + Ae^{t/2}$, where $A$ is a constant.

Applying the initial condition $p(0) = 100$ gives $100 = 200 + A$, so $A = -100$.
Thus, the particular solution is $p(t) = 200 - 100e^{t/2}$.

This corresponds to option B.

\boxed{B}

63319.subject: Mathematics
63319.text: If the equation $ax^2 + 4xy - 2y^2 + 4x + 8y + 1 = 0$ represents a pair of straight lines, then the coordinates of their point of intersection are.........
63319.sol:
The given equation is $S = ax^2 + 4xy - 2y^2 + 4x + 8y + 1 = 0$.

Comparing with the general equation of second degree $ax^2 + 2hxy + by^2 + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0$, we get:

$a = a$, $h = 2$, $b = -2$, $g = 2$, $f = 4$, $c = 1$.

For the equation to represent a pair of straight lines, the condition is $\Delta = abc + 2fgh - af^2 - bg^2 - ch^2 = 0$.

Substituting the values:

$a(-2)(1) + 2(4)(2)(2) - a(4)^2 - (-2)(2)^2 - 1(2)^2 = 0$

$-2a + 32 - 16a + 8 - 4 = 0$

$-18a + 36 = 0 \Rightarrow a = 2$

The point of intersection of the pair of straight lines is obtained by solving $\dfrac{\partial S}{\partial x} = 0 and \dfrac{\partial S}{\partial y} = 0$.

$\dfrac{\partial S}{\partial x} = 2ax + 4y + 4 = 0$

Substituting $a = 2$:

$4x + 4y + 4 = 0 \Rightarrow x + y + 1 = 0$

$\dfrac{\partial S}{\partial y} = 4x - 4y + 8 = 0 \Rightarrow x - y + 2 = 0$

Adding the two equations:

$2x + 3 = 0 \Rightarrow x = -\dfrac{3}{2}$

Subtracting the second equation from the first:

$2y - 1 = 0 \Rightarrow y = \dfrac{1}{2}$

The coordinates of the point of intersection are $\left(-\dfrac{3}{2}, \dfrac{1}{2}\right)$.

Answer: $\left(-\dfrac{3}{2}, \dfrac{1}{2}\right)$

63333.subject: Mathematics
63333.text: If the equation $x^2 - ky^2 - 4x + 6y - 5 = 0$ represents a pair of straight lines, then their point of intersection is
63333.sol:
The given equation is $x^2 - ky^2 - 4x + 6y - 5 = 0$.

Comparing this with the general second-degree equation $ax^2 + 2hxy + by^2 + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0$, we get:
$a = 1$, $h = 0$, $b = -k$, $g = -2$, $f = 3$, $c = -5$.

For the equation to represent a pair of straight lines, the condition is $abc + 2fgh - af^2 - bg^2 - ch^2 = 0$.

Substituting the values:
$(1)(-k)(-5) + 0 - (1)(3)^2 - (-k)(-2)^2 - 0 = 0$

$5k - 9 + 4k = 0$

$9k = 9 \Rightarrow k = 1$

So, the equation of the pair of straight lines is $x^2 - y^2 - 4x + 6y - 5 = 0$.

Let $F(x, y) = x^2 - y^2 - 4x + 6y - 5$.
The point of intersection of the lines is obtained by solving the partial derivatives $\dfrac{\partial F}{\partial x} = 0$ and $\dfrac{\partial F}{\partial y} = 0$.

$\dfrac{\partial F}{\partial x} = 2x - 4 = 0 \Rightarrow x = 2$

$\dfrac{\partial F}{\partial y} = -2y + 6 = 0 \Rightarrow y = 3$

The point of intersection is $(2, 3)$.

Answer: $(2, 3)$

63572.subject: Mathematics
63572.text: A box contains 8 red and N green balls. Two balls are drawn at random from it. If X is the random variable representing the number of green balls drawn and $E(X) = 1.2$, then $N = \ldots$
63572.sol:
Total number of balls $= N + 8$

Two balls are drawn at random. Let $X$ be the number of green balls drawn. The possible values of $X$ are $0, 1, 2$.

$P(X=1) = \dfrac{^{N}C_{1} \times ^{8}C_{1}}{^{N+8}C_{2}} = \dfrac{16N}{(N+8)(N+7)}$

$P(X=2) = \dfrac{^{N}C_{2}}{^{N+8}C_{2}} = \dfrac{N(N-1)}{(N+8)(N+7)}$

The expected value $E(X)$ is given by:

$E(X) = 1 \times P(X=1) + 2 \times P(X=2)$

$E(X) = \dfrac{16N + 2N(N-1)}{(N+8)(N+7)} = \dfrac{2N(N+7)}{(N+8)(N+7)} = \dfrac{2N}{N+8}$

Given $E(X) = 1.2$, we have:

$\dfrac{2N}{N+8} = 1.2$

$2N = 1.2N + 9.6$

$0.8N = 9.6$

$N = 12$

Answer: $12$

63573.subject: Mathematics
63573.text: If the mean and the variance of a binomial variate X are 1 and 0.75 respectively, then which of the following is true?
63573.sol:
Given mean $np = 1$ and variance $npq = 0.75 = \dfrac{3}{4}$.

Dividing variance by mean:

$q = \dfrac{npq}{np} = \dfrac{3}{4}$

Since $p + q = 1$, $p = 1 - \dfrac{3}{4} = \dfrac{1}{4}$.

Substituting $p$ in $np = 1$:

$n \left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right) = 1 \Rightarrow n = 4$

The probability of $X = r$ is given by $P(X = r) = ^{n}C_{r} p^r q^{n-r}$.

Calculating $P(X = 1)$ and $P(X = 2)$:

$P(X = 1) = ^{4}C_{1} \left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)^1 \left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right)^3 = 4 \times \dfrac{1}{4} \times \dfrac{27}{64} = \dfrac{27}{64}$

$P(X = 2) = ^{4}C_{2} \left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)^2 \left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right)^2 = 6 \times \dfrac{1}{16} \times \dfrac{9}{16} = \dfrac{54}{256} = \dfrac{27}{128}$

Comparing the two probabilities:

$2P(X = 2) = 2 \times \dfrac{27}{128} = \dfrac{27}{64} = P(X = 1)$

Thus, $P(X = 1) = 2P(X = 2)$.

Answer: $P(X = 1) = 2P(X = 2)$

64462.text: If the lines $\frac{x-1}{2}=\frac{y+1}{k}=\frac{z}{2}$ and $\frac{x+1}{5}=\frac{y+1}{2}=\frac{z}{k}$ are coplanar, then the equation of the plane containing these lines are
64462.sol:
Lines $L_1$ and $L_2$ are coplanar if the scalar triple product $\vec{AB} \cdot (\vec{d_1} \times \vec{d_2}) = 0$, where $A(1,-1,0)$ and $B(-1,-1,0)$ are points on each line, and $\vec{d_1} = (2,k,2)$, $\vec{d_2} = (5,2,k)$ are their direction vectors.

The vector $\vec{AB} = (-2,0,0)$, so the determinant condition is:

\begin{vmatrix} -2 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & k & 2 \\ 5 & 2 & k \end{vmatrix} = 0$

Expanding gives $-2(k^2 - 4) = 0$, so $k^2 = 4$ and $k = \pm 2$.

For $k = 2$, the direction vectors are \vec{d_1} = (1,1,1)$ and $\vec{d_2} = (5,2,2)$. The normal vector $\vec{n} = \vec{d_1} \times \vec{d_2} = (0,3,-3) \propto (0,1,-1)$, yielding the plane equation $y - z + 1 = 0$.

For $k = -2$, $\vec{d_1} = (1,-1,1)$ and $\vec{d_2} = (5,2,-2)$. Then $\vec{n} = (0,7,7) \propto (0,1,1)$, giving $y + z + 1 = 0$.

The two planes are $y \pm z + 1 = 0$, corresponding to option B.

65081.text: If the volume of the tetrahedron whose coterminous edges are given by the vectors $\bar{a} = -2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} - 3\hat{k}$, $\bar{b} = 4\hat{i} + 5\hat{j} + (\lambda - 10)\hat{k}$, $\bar{c} = 6\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - 3\hat{k}$ is 11 cubic units, then the sum of the possible values of $\lambda$ is $\ldots$
65081.sol:
The volume of a tetrahedron with coterminous edges $\bar{a}$, $\bar{b}$, $\bar{c}$ is given by $V = \dfrac{1}{6} |[\bar{a}, \bar{b}, \bar{c}]|$.

Given $V = 11$, we have $|[\bar{a}, \bar{b}, \bar{c}]| = 66$.

Calculating the scalar triple product:

$[\bar{a}, \bar{b}, \bar{c}] = \begin{vmatrix} -2 \text{ and } 3 \text{ and } -3 \\ 4 \text{ and } 5 \text{ and } \lambda - 10 \\ 6 \text{ and } 2 \text{ and } -3 \end{vmatrix}$

$= -2(-15 - 2(\lambda - 10)) - 3(-12 - 6(\lambda - 10)) - 3(8 - 30)$

$= -2(5 - 2\lambda) - 3(48 - 6\lambda) - 3(-22)$

$= -10 + 4\lambda - 144 + 18\lambda + 66$

$= 22\lambda - 88$

Substituting this into the volume equation:

$|22\lambda - 88| = 66$

$22|\lambda - 4| = 66$

$|\lambda - 4| = 3$

This gives $\lambda - 4 = 3 \Rightarrow \lambda = 7$ and $\lambda - 4 = -3 \Rightarrow \lambda = 1$.

The possible values of $\lambda$ are $7$ and $1$.

The sum of the possible values of $\lambda$ is $7 + 1 = 8$.

Answer: $8$

65197.sol:
Given vectors $\bar{a} = 4\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} + \hat{k}$ and $\bar{b} = \hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$, the dot product is $\bar{a} \cdot \bar{b} = (4)(1) + (3)(-2) + (1)(2) = 0$, confirming orthogonality.

The magnitude squared is $|\bar{a}|^2 = 4^2 + 3^2 + 1^2 = 26$.

Evaluating the nested cross product $\bar{a} \times (\bar{a} \times (\bar{a} \times (\bar{a} \times \bar{b})))$
Using the vector triple product identity $\bar{x} \times (\bar{y} \times \bar{z}) = (\bar{x} \cdot \bar{z})\bar{y} - (\bar{x} \cdot \bar{y})\bar{z}$:

Let $\bar{v}_2 = \bar{a} \times (\bar{a} \times \bar{b}) = (\bar{a} \cdot \bar{b})\bar{a} - (\bar{a} \cdot \bar{a})\bar{b} = -26\bar{b}$.

Then $\bar{v}_3 = \bar{a} \times \bar{v}_2 = \bar{a} \times (-26\bar{b}) = -26(\bar{a} \times \bar{b})$.

Finally, $\bar{v}_4 = \bar{a} \times \bar{v}_3 = \bar{a} \times (-26\bar{v}_1) = -26(\bar{a} \times \bar{v}_1) = -26(-26\bar{b}) = 676\bar{b}$.

The result simplifies to $676\bar{b}$.

68154.text: The amount of work done in blowing a soap bubble such that its diameter increases from $d_1$ to $d_2$ is (T=$ surface tension of soap solution)$
68154.sol:
The work done equals the change in surface energy, given by $W = T \Delta A$, where $T$ is the surface tension and $\Delta A$ the area difference.

A soap bubble has two surfaces, so its total area is $8 \pi R^2$.

Given initial diameter $d_1$ and final $d_2$, radii are $R_1 = d_1 / 2$ and $R_2 = d_2 / 2$.

Initial area is $A_1 = 8 \pi (d_1 / 2)^2 = 2 \pi d_1^2$, final area $A_2 = 8 \pi (d_2 / 2)^2 = 2 \pi d_2^2$, so $\Delta A = 2 \pi (d_2^2 - d_1^2)$.

Therefore, work done is $W = T \cdot 2 \pi (d_2^2 - d_1^2) = 2 \pi T (d_2^2 - d_1^2)$.

This corresponds to option D.

69174.text: Let M and L be the mass and length of thin uniform rod respectively. In first case, axis of rotation is passing through centre and perpendicular to length of rod. Moment of inertia of a thin uniform rod about an axis passing through its centre and perpendicular to its length is $I_1 = \dfrac{ML^2}{12}$.

69399.subject: Physics
69399.text: The depletion region of p-n junction
options: remains same in reverse and forward biasing.
69399.sol:
In a p-n junction, when it is reverse biased, the positive terminal of the battery is connected to the n-type region and the negative terminal to the p-type region.

The applied reverse voltage is in the same direction as the built-in potential barrier. This increases the effective potential barrier across the junction.

As a result, the majority charge carriers are pulled away from the junction, which causes the width of the depletion region to increase.

Conversely, during forward biasing, the applied voltage opposes the built-in potential, causing the depletion region to decrease.

Answer: increases if reverse biased.

69457.subject: Physics
69457.text: The material used for solar cell should have band gap
69457.sol:
The efficiency of a solar cell is highly dependent on the semiconductor's band gap, $E_g$. Photons with $E_{\text{photon}} < E_g$ are not absorbed and contribute no current, while those with $E_{\text{photon}} > E_g$ are absorbed but lose excess energy as heat through thermalization.

A small band gap (e.g., < $1.0$ eV) leads to high photon absorption but low output voltage and significant dark current. A large band gap (e.g., > $1.8$ eV) limits absorption to high-energy photons, wasting much of the solar spectrum.

The optimal range for single-junction solar cells is $1.0$ eV to $1.8$ eV, balancing absorption and voltage efficiency. Silicon, with $E_g \approx 1.12$ eV, is widely used due to its placement within this range.

Therefore, the material should have a band gap between $1.0$ eV and $1.8$ eV, corresponding to option $\boxed{\text{D}}$.

69485.subject: Physics
69485.text: For an ideal diode, in forward and reverse biased condition the resistance is respectively
69485.sol:
An ideal diode exhibits perfect conduction under forward bias and perfect insulation under reverse bias.

When forward biased, the diode behaves as a perfect conductor with zero voltage drop. Applying Ohm's law $R=V/I$, since $V=0$ for any non-zero current $I$, the resistance is zero.

When reverse biased, the diode acts as a perfect insulator with zero current flow. Again applying $R=V/I$, since $I=0$ for any non-zero voltage $V$, the resistance is infinite.

Conclusion: Forward bias resistance is zero, reverse bias resistance is infinite.

Among the options:
A) infinite, zero (incorrect)
B) infinite, infinite (incorrect)
C) zero, zero (incorrect)
D) zero, infinite (correct)

The correct answer is D.

71124.subject: Biology
71124.text: Convulsions, anaemia, hepatomegaly etc. are the symptoms of ________.
71124.sol:
Malaria is caused by the Plasmodium parasite, which infects and destroys red blood cells, leading to anaemia. The infection also causes the liver and spleen to enlarge, resulting in hepatomegaly and splenomegaly. In severe cases, particularly with Plasmodium falciparum (cerebral malaria), it can affect the brain and cause neurological symptoms such as convulsions.

Pneumonia primarily affects the lungs, causing cough and difficulty breathing. Typhoid causes sustained high fever, weakness, and intestinal issues. The common cold affects the upper respiratory tract.

Answer: malaria

72205.subject: Physics
72205.text: Two point charges $+8q$ and $-2q$ are located at $x=0$ and $x=L$ respectively. What is the location of a point on the x-axis from the origin, at which the net electric field due to these two point charges is zero?
72205.sol:
Let the point where the net electric field is zero be at a distance $x$ from the origin on the x-axis.

Since the charges have opposite signs, the null point must lie outside the region between the charges and closer to the charge with the smaller magnitude. Thus, the point lies at $x > L$.

Equating the magnitudes of the electric fields due to both charges at this point:

$\dfrac{k(8q)}{x^2} = \dfrac{k(2q)}{(x-L)^2}$

$\dfrac{4}{x^2} = \dfrac{1}{(x-L)^2}$

Taking the square root on both sides:

$\dfrac{2}{x} = \dfrac{1}{x-L}$

$2x - 2L = x$

$x = 2L$

Answer: $2L$

72240.text: The Translational K.E. of the molecules of a gas at absolute temperature (T) can be doubled by
72240.sol:
The average translational kinetic energy of a gas molecule is given by $E = \dfrac{3}{2} k_B T$.

This shows that the translational kinetic energy is directly proportional to the absolute temperature of the gas, i.e., $E \propto T$.

To double the translational kinetic energy, the absolute temperature must be doubled.

Therefore, the temperature should be increased to $2T$.

Answer: increasing T to 2 T

76368.text:
For the following three (03) items:
Consider the function $f(x) = x|x|$.

Consider the following statements:
I. The function is increasing in the interval $(-\infty, \infty)$.
II. The function is differentiable at $x = 0$.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
76368.sol:
The given function is $f(x) = x|x|$.

This can be redefined as:
$f(x) = x^2$ for $x \ge 0$
$f(x) = -x^2$ for $x < 0$

Differentiating with respect to $x$, we get:
$f'(x) = 2x$ for $x > 0$
$f'(x) = -2x$ for $x < 0$

At $x = 0$, the left-hand derivative is $\lim_{h \to 0^-} \dfrac{-h^2 - 0}{h} = 0$ and the right-hand derivative is $\lim_{h \to 0^+} \dfrac{h^2 - 0}{h} = 0$.

Since the left-hand derivative equals the right-hand derivative, $f(x)$ is differentiable at $x = 0$. Thus, statement II is correct.

Also, $f'(x) = 2|x| \ge 0$ for all $x \in (-\infty, \infty)$. Since $f'(x) > 0$ for all $x \neq 0$ and $f(x)$ is continuous, the function is strictly increasing in $(-\infty, \infty)$. Thus, statement I is correct.

Both statements I and II are correct.

Answer: Both I and II

77996.text:
Consider the following for the two (02) items that follow:
The probabilities that $A$, $B$ and $C$ become managers are $\dfrac{3}{10}$, $\dfrac{1}{2}$ and $\dfrac{4}{5}$ respectively. The probabilities that bonus scheme will be introduced if $A$, $B$ and $C$ become managers are $\dfrac{4}{9}$, $\dfrac{2}{9}$ and $\dfrac{1}{3}$ respectively.

What is the probability that the bonus scheme will be introduced?
77996.sol:
Let $E_1$, $E_2$, and $E_3$ be the events that $A$, $B$, and $C$ become managers respectively.

The given probabilities are:
$P(E_1) = \dfrac{3}{10}$
$P(E_2) = \dfrac{1}{2}$
$P(E_3) = \dfrac{4}{5}$

Let $S$ be the event that the bonus scheme is introduced. The conditional probabilities are:
$P(S|E_1) = \dfrac{4}{9}$
$P(S|E_2) = \dfrac{2}{9}$
$P(S|E_3) = \dfrac{1}{3}$

Using the law of total probability, the probability that the bonus scheme will be introduced is:
$P(S) = P(E_1)P(S|E_1) + P(E_2)P(S|E_2) + P(E_3)P(S|E_3)$

Substituting the given values:
$P(S) = \left(\dfrac{3}{10} \times \dfrac{4}{9}\right) + \left(\dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{2}{9}\right) + \left(\dfrac{4}{5} \times \dfrac{1}{3}\right)

$P(S) = $\dfrac{12}{90} + \dfrac{2}{18} + \dfrac{4}{15}

$ P(S) = $\dfrac{2}{15} + \dfrac{1}{9} + \dfrac{4}{15}

$ P(S) = $\dfrac{6}{15} + \dfrac{1}{9}

$ P(S) = $\dfrac{2}{5} + \dfrac{1}{9}

$ P(S) = $\dfrac{18 + 5}{45} = \dfrac{23}{45}$$

Answer: $$\dfrac{23}{45}$

83276.text: A mass falls from a height ' $h$ ' and its time of fall ' $t$ ' is recorded in terms of time period $T$ of a simple pendulum. On the surface of earth it is found that $t=2 \mathrm{~T}$. The distance covered by the mass falling from height ' $h$ ' during its time of fall ' $t$ ' is given by

$\begin{array}{r}$$\mathrm{s}=\mathrm{h}=\mathrm{ut}+\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{gt}^$2 \\
$\text{ As, } \mathrm{u}=$0 \Rightarrow $\mathrm{h}=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{gt}^$2 \Rightarrow $\mathrm{t}=\sqrt{\frac{2 \mathrm{~h}}{\mathrm{~g}}}

$\mathrm{T}=$2 $\pi \sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{l}}{\mathrm{g}}}$where, lis the length of the pendulum. From Eq. (i) and (ii), since ' $h$ ' and ' $l$ ' are constant so, we can conclude that,

$\mathrm{t} \propto \frac{\mathrm{l}}{\sqrt{\mathrm{g}}} \text{ and } \mathrm{T} \propto \frac{\mathrm{l}}{\sqrt{\mathrm{g}}} \quad \therefore \frac{\mathrm{t}}{\mathrm{T}}=\mathrm{l}$Thus, the ratio of time of fall and time period of pendulum is independent of value of gravity $(\mathrm{g})$ or any other parameter like mass and radius of the planet. Thus, the relation between $\mathrmt^{\prime}$ and $\mathrm{T}^{\prime}$ on another planet irrespective of its mass or radius will remains same as it was on earth i.e.

\mathrmt^{\prime}=2 $\mathrm{~T}^{\prime}$

83674.subject: Physics
83674.text:
In an adiabatic expansion, the temperature of one mole of an ideal monatomic gas ($\gamma=5/3$) decreases from $60$K to $50$K. The work done by the gas in the process is :
(Take the universal gas constant as $R=8.3$ J mol$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$)
83674.sol:
The work done by an ideal gas in an adiabatic process is given by the formula:

$W = \dfrac{nR(T_1 - T_2)}{\gamma - 1}$

Given values are:
$n = 1$ mole
$R = 8.3$ J mol$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$
$T_1 = 60$ K
$T_2 = 50$ K
$\gamma = \dfrac{5}{3}$

Substituting these values into the formula:

$W = \dfrac{1 \times 8.3 \times (60 - 50)}{\dfrac{5}{3} - 1}$

$W = \dfrac{8.3 \times 10}{\dfrac{2}{3}}$

$W = \dfrac{83 \times 3}{2}$

$W = \dfrac{249}{2} = 124.5$ J

Answer: $124.5$ J

84445.subject: Zoology
84445.text:
The following are the stages of life cycle of Plasmodium. Arrange the stages in the proper order.
A. The parasites reproduce asexually in RBCs, bursting the cells.
B. The parasites reproduce asexually in liver cells, bursting the cells and releasing into blood.
C. Gametocytes develop in RBCs.
D. Sporozoites reach the liver through the blood.
E. Female mosquito injects sporozoites into humans during bite.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
84445.sol:
The life cycle of Plasmodium in the human body follows a specific sequence:

First, an infected female Anopheles mosquito bites a human and injects the infective form, known as sporozoites, into the human body (E).

These sporozoites travel through the bloodstream and reach the liver (D).

Inside the liver cells, the parasites multiply asexually, eventually bursting the liver cells and releasing the newly formed parasites (merozoites) into the blood (B).

The released parasites then enter the red blood cells (RBCs) where they continue to reproduce asexually. This causes the RBCs to burst, releasing toxic substances (hemozoin) responsible for the characteristic chills and high fever (A).

Finally, some of the parasites in the RBCs differentiate into the sexual stages called gametocytes (C), which are later taken up by a mosquito during a blood meal to continue the cycle.

Thus, the correct sequence is E, D, B, A, C.

Answer: E, D, B, A, C

84638.sol:
Spermatogonia $\rightarrow$ Spermatocyte $\rightarrow$ Spermatid $\rightarrow$ Spermatozoa

84740.subject: Zoology
84740.text: Which one of the following is the correct description of a certain part of a normal human skeleton?
options: Parietal bone and the temporal bone of the skull are joined by fibrous joint
First vertebra is axis, which articulates with the occipital condyles
The $9^{\text{th }}$ and $10^{\text{th }}$ pairs of ribs are called the floating ribs
Glenoid cavity is a depression to which the thigh bone articulates
84740.sol:
Immovable or fixed or fibrous joints are found between the skull bones. No movement occurs at these joints. So, parietal bone and the temporal bone of the skull are joined by fibrous joint. 
Invertebrates, the first vertebra is called atlas, while the second vertebra is axis. In humans, first seven pairs of ribs are called true rubs; $8^{\text{th }}, 9^{\text{th }}$ and $10^{\text{th }}$ pairs of ribs are false ribs while $11^{\text{th }}$ and $12^{\text{th }}$ pairs of ribs are called floating ribs.
Glenoid cavity is a socket-shaped cavity in the scapula (shoulder bone) that holds the head of the humerus in a ball and socket joint.

85456.chapter: Strategies for Enhancement in Food Production
85456.text: In order to obtain virus-free plants through tissue culture the best method is:
85456.sol:
The virus infected plants only the meristematic cells of the apical dome are devoid of virus. Therefore, by using shoot apical meristem culture, virus free plants can be raised.
Related Theory
In the meristem there is no cells differentiation. Virus can't move from cell to cell through plasmodesmesta using their Movement protein.
Meristematic cells are considered as virus free because:
(1) Meristematic cells have high multiplication rate than viral cell multiplication rates.
(2) Viruses generally move in plant body through vascular bundles. There is the absence of vascular bundles in meristematic regions.
(3) High auxin concentration and cytokinin concentration and low pH value at which viruses could not survive.
(4) High metabolic activity.
(5) RNA silencing mechanism. According to some findings, it has been hypothesized that the defense systems in meristematic regions treat viruses as foreign particles thus prevent the viruses into the meristematic regions.

90955.text: The area (in sq. units) of the triangle formed by the lines $y = 2x, y = - 2x$ and the tangent at the point $\left(\sqrt{5}, 4\right)$ on $4x^{2} - y^{2} = 4$ is equal to

Equation of the tangent at point $\left(\sqrt{5}, 4\right)$ on $4x^{2} - y^{2} = 4$ is $4x\sqrt{5} - 4y = 4 ⇒ \sqrt{5}x - y = 1$.
Now, point of intersection of $y = \sqrt{5}x - 1 & y = 2x$ is $\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{5} - 2}, \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{5} - 2}\right)$.
Point of intersection of $y = \sqrt{5}x - 1$ and $y = - 2x$ is& $\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{5} + 2}, \dfrac{- 2}{\sqrt{5} + 2}\right) .$
Point of intersection of $y = 2x$ & $y = - 2x$ is $\left(0,0\right)$
Now, area of the triangle formed by the points $\left(0,0\right), \left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{5} - 2}, \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{5} - 2}\right), \left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{5} + 2}, \dfrac{- 2}{\sqrt{5} + 2}\right)
$= $\left|\dfrac{1}{2}\left|\begin{cases}0 & 0 & 1 \\ 1\left(\sqrt{5} -2\right) & 2\left(\sqrt{5} -2\right) & 1 \\ 1\left(\sqrt{5} +2\right) & - 2\left(\sqrt{5} +2\right) & 1\end{cases}\right|\right| = \left|\dfrac{1}{2} \times1 \times \left(-2 - 2\right)\right| = 2$& sq.units

91631.text: A person goes to the office either by a car, or scooter, or bus, the probability of which being $\dfrac{2}{7}, \dfrac{3}{7}, \dfrac{2}{7}$ respectively. 91631.sol:
Let, $C, B, S$ be the events such that a person goes to the office by car, bus or scooter respectively.
$P\left(C\right) = \dfrac{2}{7}, P\left(S\right) = \dfrac{3}{7}, P\left(B\right) = \dfrac{2}{7}$
Let, $T$ be the event that he reaches office in time
$P\left(\dfrac{T}{C}\right) = \dfrac{7}{9}, P\left(\dfrac{T}{S}\right) = \dfrac{8}{9}, P\left(\dfrac{T}{B}\right) = \dfrac{5}{9}$
$P\left(\dfrac{C}{T}\right) = \dfrac{P\left(C\right)P\left(\dfrac{T}{C}\right)}{P\left(C\right)P\left(\dfrac{T}{C}\right) + P\left(B\right)P\left(\dfrac{T}{B}\right) + P\left(S\right)P\left(\dfrac{T}{S}\right)}$
$= \dfrac{\dfrac{2}{7} \times \dfrac{7}{9}}{\dfrac{2}{7} \times \dfrac{7}{9} + \dfrac{3}{7} \times \dfrac{8}{9} + \dfrac{2}{7} \times \dfrac{5}{9}} = \dfrac{14}{48} = \dfrac{7}{24}$

Putting the value and solving we get $x = 2$ cm

95658.subject: Botany
95658.text: Which of the following can be used in the filtration of oils and syrups?
95658.sol: In diatoms, the cell walls form two thin overlapping shells, which fit together as in a soapbox. The walls are embedded with silica and thus the walls are indestructible. Thus, diatoms have left behind large amounts of cell wall deposits in their habitat; this accumulation over billions of years is referred to as ‘diatomaceous earth’. Being gritty, this soil is used in polishing and filtration of oils and syrups.

95665.subject: Botany
95665.text: In which of the following, asexual spores are generally not seen, but there is the development of a dikaryophase stage?
95665.sol:
When a fungus reproduces sexually, two haploid hyphae of compatible mating types come together and fuse.

In ascomycetes and basidiomycetes, the fusion of two haploid cells forms an intermediate stage called the dikaryotic stage. In this stage, one cell has two diploid nuclei. This stage is called dikaryophase. Later, the parental nuclei fuse, and the cells become diploid. Asexual spores are generally not seen in basidiomycetes, and they generally undergo fragmentation. Thus, basidiomycetes is the group in which asexual spores are generally not seen but dikaryophase is seen. Albugo belongs to phycomycetes, Claviceps belongs to ascomycetes, Alternaria belongs to deuteromycetes, and Agaricus (mushroom) belongs to basidiomycetes.

I. Chromosomes migrate to opposite poles of the spindle.
II. Chromosomes arrange themselves at the equator of the spindle.
III. Chromosomes condense and the nuclear membrane disappears.

100353.subject: Physics
100353.text:
Match the initial and final directions of a car moving at a constant speed (List-I) with the direction of the average force acting on it during the turn (List-II).

List-IList-II
(A) Moving North, turns East(I) North-West
(B) Moving East, turns South(II) North-East
(C) Moving South, turns West(III) South-West
(D) Moving West, turns North(IV) South-East

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
100353.sol:
The direction of the average force is the same as the direction of the change in velocity, $\Delta\vec{v} = \vec{v}_f - \vec{v}_i$.

Let the speed be $v$. We take East as $\hat{i}$, North as $\hat{j}$, West as $-\hat{i}$, and South as $-\hat{j}$.

(A) Moving North ($\vec{v}_i = v\hat{j}$), turns East ($\vec{v}_f = v\hat{i}$).
$\Delta\vec{v} = v\hat{i} - v\hat{j}$ (South-East). So, (A) matches (IV).

(B) Moving East ($\vec{v}_i = v\hat{i}$), turns South ($\vec{v}_f = -v\hat{j}$).
$\Delta\vec{v} = -v\hat{j} - v\hat{i}$ (South-West). So, (B) matches (III).

(C) Moving South ($\vec{v}_i = -v\hat{j}$), turns West ($\vec{v}_f = -v\hat{i}$).
$\Delta\vec{v} = -v\hat{i} - (-v\hat{j}) = -v\hat{i} + v\hat{j}$ (North-West). So, (C) matches (I).

(D) Moving West ($\vec{v}_i = -v\hat{i}$), turns North ($\vec{v}_f = v\hat{j}$).
$\Delta\vec{v} = v\hat{j} - (-v\hat{i}) = v\hat{i} + v\hat{j}$ (North-East). So, (D) matches (II).

The correct matching is (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(I), (D)-(II).

Answer: (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(I), (D)-(II)
100353.meta: Match the initial and final directions of a car moving at a constant speed (List-I) with the direction of the average force acting on it during the turn

100960.subject: Physics
100960.text: Two blocks of masses $m_1$ and $m_2$ are connected by a spring of spring constant $k$. The block of mass $m_2$ is given a sharp empulse so that it acquires a velocity $v_0$ towards right. Find the maximum elongation that the spring will suffer.
100960.sol:
The velocity of centre of mass
$v_{\mathrm{cm}}=\frac{m_1 v_1+m_2 v_2}{m_1+m_2}$
When $v_1=0$ and $v_2=v_0$, then
$v_{c m}=\frac{m_2 v_0}{m_1+m_2}$
Now, let $x$ be the elongation in the spring.
Change in potential energy $=$ potential energy stored in spring
$\begin{gathered}
\Rightarrow \quad \frac{1}{2} m_2 v_0^2-\frac{1}{2}\left(m_1+m_2\right) \\
\left(\frac{m_2 V_0}{m_1+m_2}\right)^2=\frac{1}{2} k x^2
\end{gathered}$
This gives, $x=\left(\frac{m_1 m_2}{m_1+m_2}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}} v_0$

101701.subject: Physics
101701.text: The variation of absolute pressure $P$ with depth $h$ below the free surface of an unknown liquid is plotted on a graph. The graph is a straight line that gives $P = 1 \times 10^5$ Pa at $h = 0$ m, and $P = 2.2 \times 10^5$ Pa at $h = 10$ m. Assuming the acceleration due to gravity $g = 10$ m/s$^2$, what is the density of the liquid?
101701.sol:
The absolute pressure $P$ at a depth $h$ is given by the equation:
$P = P_{atm} + \rho g h$

This represents a linear equation of the form $y = c + mx$, where the slope of the $P$ versus $h$ graph is $m = \rho g$.

From the given data, the slope is:
$\dfrac{\Delta P}{\Delta h} = \dfrac{2.2 \times 10^5 - 1 \times 10^5}{10 - 0}$
$\dfrac{\Delta P}{\Delta h} = \dfrac{1.2 \times 10^5}{10} = 1.2 \times 10^4$ Pa/m

Equating this slope to $\rho g$:
$\rho g = 1.2 \times 10^4$
$\rho \times 10 = 12000$
$\rho = 1200$ kg/m$^3$

Using $P/h$ at $h=10$ without subtracting the intercept leads to the incorrect $2200$ kg/m$^3$.

Answer: $1200$ kg/m$^3$

102405.subject: Physics
102405.text: Two simple pendulums of lengths $l_1 and l_2$ are oscillating with small angular amplitudes $\theta_1$ and $\theta_2$, respectively. If their maximum linear speeds at their lowest points are exactly equal, the ratio of their angular amplitudes $\left(\dfrac{\theta_1}{\theta_2}\right)$ is:
102405.sol:
For a simple pendulum of length $l$ oscillating with a small angular amplitude $\theta_0$, the linear amplitude is $A = l\theta_0$.

The angular frequency of the simple pendulum is $\omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{g}{l}}$.

The maximum linear speed of the pendulum bob is given by $v_{\max} = A\omega$.

Substituting the expressions for $A$ and $\omega$:
$v_{\max} = (l\theta_0)\sqrt{\dfrac{g}{l}} = \theta_0\sqrt{gl}$

Given that the maximum linear speeds of the two pendulums are equal:
$\theta_1\sqrt{gl_1} = \theta_2\sqrt{gl_2}$

Rearranging to find the ratio of their angular amplitudes:
$\dfrac{\theta_1}{\theta_2} = \dfrac{\sqrt{l_2}}{\sqrt{l_1}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{l_2}{l_1}}$

102431.subject: Physics
102431.text: A particle executes Simple Harmonic Motion in the $xy$-plane along a straight line given by the equation $y = \sqrt{3}x$. The mean position of the particle is at the origin, and the total amplitude of its motion is $A_0$. What are the amplitudes of the SHM components along the $x$-axis and $y$-axis respectively?
102431.sol:
The path of the particle is a straight line given by $y = \sqrt{3}x$.

Comparing this with the general equation of a straight line passing through the origin $y = (\tan \theta)x$, we get $\tan \theta = \sqrt{3}$. This means the line makes an angle $\theta = 60^{\circ}$ with the positive $x$-axis.

The total amplitude $A_0$ is directed along this straight line path. The component of the amplitude along the $x$-axis is:
$A_x = A_0 \cos 60^{\circ} = A_0 \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = \dfrac{A_0}{2}$

The component of the amplitude along the $y$-axis is:
$A_y = A_0 \sin 60^{\circ} = A_0 \left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}A_0}{2}$

Thus, the amplitudes along the $x$-axis and $y$-axis are $\dfrac{A_0}{2}$ and $\dfrac{\sqrt{3}A_0}{2}$ respectively.

Answer: $\dfrac{A_0}{2}$ and $\dfrac{\sqrt{3}A_0}{2}$

108651.subject: Chemistry
108651.text: An ideal gas undergoes an expansion from volume $V_1$ to $V_2$ ($V_2 > V_1$). During this process, it is observed that the heat exchange with the surroundings is zero ($q = 0$) and the change in temperature of the gas is also zero ($\Delta T = 0$). Under which of the following conditions did this expansion occur?
108651.sol:
For an ideal gas, the change in internal energy ($\Delta U$) depends only on the change in temperature ($\Delta T$). Since it is given that $\Delta T = 0$, it follows that $\Delta U = 0$.

The problem also states that the heat exchange $q = 0$.

Applying the first law of thermodynamics, $\Delta U = q + w$. Substituting the known values gives $0 = 0 + w$, which means the work done $w = 0$.

The work done during expansion is given by $w = -P_{\text{ext}} \Delta V$. Since the gas undergoes expansion ($V_2 > V_1$, so $\Delta V > 0$) and $w = 0$, the external pressure $P_{\text{ext}}$ must be zero.

An expansion where the external pressure is zero is known as free expansion, which occurs when a gas expands against a vacuum.

In a reversible adiabatic expansion, temperature decreases. In a reversible isothermal expansion, heat must be absorbed to do work. An isochoric process cannot involve an increase in volume.

Answer: Expansion against a vacuum
